title: The Missing Will
premise: When a body is discovered on the marsh road outside Harrow Bay dressed in clothing stolen from her own closet, true-crime podcaster Lena Sterling realizes the victim is wearing the exact outfit described in a thirty-year-old witness statement — one she helped archive as a teenager. The dead man is the estranged brother of the man convicted in the town's only murder, and the missing will he carried could have freed him. As Lena reopens the case on air, she uncovers that the original alibis were woven together by the very people who raised her, and that her beloved foster mother orchestrated the cover-up. At trial, Lena chooses truth over loyalty, testifying to what she saw as a child; the conviction is vacated, her foster mother is charged, and Lena rebuilds her found family on honest ground, adopting the exonerated man's quiet ritual of Sunday dinners.
about_author: Odile Almeida is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep and the cost of finally saying them out loud.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Recording a mundane episode about Harrow Bay history, Lena is called to the marsh road where a body wears her own archived outfit — the one from the 1994 witness statement. Detective Ruiz, an old source, lets her see the scene. The beat is dread: her meticulous filing has just made her a witness in her own story.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In her archive, Lena finds the 1994 statement matching the clothes, signed by her foster mother, Marisol Vane. The victim is Danny Okafor, brother of convicted murderer Elias Okafor. A threatening note appears in her mailbox. The beat is unease as the past begins rearranging itself around her.

chapters.title: Episode One: The Man Who Stayed Guilty
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with Elias's letters in flashback. Lena airs a special episode reopening the Okafor case; downloads explode, and townspeople split between gratitude and fury. Elias writes from prison for the first time in years. The beat is purpose — Lena feels the case waking up, and so does the town.

chapters.title: The Alibi Quilt
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and Ruiz POVs. Ruiz shares the original alibis: five witnesses, all connected to Marisol, each confirming the other. Lena maps the quilt and finds a sixteenth name redacted from every record — her own. The beat is vertigo as she realizes she was part of the cover-up's architecture.

chapters.title: What the Child Saw
chapters.summary: Lena's POV with fragmented childhood flashbacks. Memory returns in pieces: a night in 1994, a car, a man in the Vane kitchen, Marisol burning papers while telling young Lena she'd 'seen nothing.' Lena confronts the gap between the mother who raised her and the woman in her memories. The beat is grief.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wouldn't Stay Buried
chapters.summary: Ruiz's POV. A sixth witness, retired nurse Cora Blum, surfaces alive in a care home and admits she was paid to lie. Before Ruiz can get a formal statement, Cora's room is ransacked and she vanishes. The beat is panic — the cover-up is killing again to stay buried.

chapters.title: Sunday Dinner with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Marisol invites Lena to Sunday dinner, and over pot roast delivers a loving, chilling speech about what families owe each other, revealing she knows about the podcast episode and Cora Blum. Lena keeps her face still and lies for the first time to the woman who taught her never to lie. The beat is heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Missing Will, Found
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and Ruiz. Following Danny Okafor's last movements, they find the will hidden in the archive itself — Marisol's donation to the historical society was a dead drop. It names a second beneficiary and proves the 1994 murder was about land and money. Marisol is arrested; Cora Blum is found alive, hidden by an ally. The beat is grim triumph.

chapters.title: The Trial of Lena Sterling
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the stand, Lena testifies to what she saw as a child, gutting the defense and devastating Marisol, who mouths 'you were mine' as she's led out. Elias watches from the gallery. The beat is sacrifice — truth costs Lena the only mother she's known, and she pays it in a steady voice.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue six months later. The conviction vacated, Elias is freed; he and Lena, strangers bound by the same stolen decades, begin Sunday dinners together. The final episode of her podcast closes the case and opens a new one — someone else's missing will. The beat is cautious hope: found family rebuilt on truth.
